title: Omega-3 and DHA in Pregnancy: Food Sources and Supplement Cautions
excerpt: The role of DHA, low-mercury fish options, and when to ask a clinician about supplements
content:
## Introduction
Omega-3 and DHA are essential nutrients for the health of both mother and baby during pregnancy. DHA (docosahexaenoic acid) is a type of omega-3 fatty acid that plays a crucial role in the development of the baby's brain and eyes. In this article, we will explore the role of DHA, food sources rich in DHA, and precautions to take when using supplements.

## The Role of DHA
DHA is an essential nutrient for the development of the baby's brain and eyes. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), DHA plays a crucial role in supporting the development of the baby's brain and eyes, particularly during the early stages of pregnancy. Additionally, DHA may also help reduce the risk of conditions such as asthma, eczema, and digestive problems.

## Food Sources Rich in DHA
There are several food sources rich in DHA that pregnant women can incorporate into their diet. Some of these sources include:
- Salmon: Salmon is a rich source of DHA and can be cooked in a variety of ways.
- Sardines: Sardines are another rich source of DHA and can be cooked in a variety of ways.
- Anchovies: Anchovies are a rich source of DHA and can be cooked in a variety of ways.
- Caviar: Caviar is a rich source of DHA and can be eaten as a snack or used as a topping for dishes.
- Seaweed: Seaweed is a rich source of DHA and can be incorporated into the diet in a variety of ways.

## Precautions to Take When Using Supplements
While DHA supplements can be a good option for pregnant women, there are several precautions to take before using them. Firstly, pregnant women should consult with their healthcare provider before taking any supplements. Additionally, pregnant women should be aware of the source and quality of the supplement to ensure it is safe for consumption.

## Sample Meal Plan
Here are some sample meal ideas that are rich in DHA:
- Breakfast: Scrambled eggs with smoked salmon
- Lunch: Grilled sardines with a side of mixed greens
- Dinner: Baked anchovies with a side of quinoa and steamed vegetables

## Conclusion
DHA is an essential nutrient for the health of both mother and baby during pregnancy. Pregnant women can incorporate DHA into their diet through food sources such as salmon, sardines, anchovies, caviar, and seaweed. However, it is essential to be aware of the source and quality of supplements and to consult with a healthcare provider before taking any. To learn more about food sources rich in DHA and how to cook them safely, pregnant women can visit our [meal planner page](/planner) or [read more about related topics](/blog/topics).

## When to Consult a Healthcare Provider
Pregnant women should consult with their healthcare provider before taking any DHA supplements, particularly if they have any underlying health conditions. Additionally, pregnant women should consult with their healthcare provider about how to cook DHA-rich foods safely and about the source and quality of supplements.
